title: AgentVQA finds visual-state tracking limits in multimodal agents
dek: An offline benchmark spans five interactive domains and isolates grounding failures that task-success scores can obscure.
evidence: Original benchmark paper; offline multiple-choice proxy for online execution
takeaway: Evaluate temporal state and object grounding before attributing multimodal agent failures to planning.

sections.title: Design

bullets.detail: The authors manually selected 1,000 cases from 23 datasets across web agents, robotics, egocentric video, games and spatial planning.
The best of 22 evaluated models reached 58.5% accuracy. Error analysis emphasized UI localization, motion interpretation, evolving state and 3D relationships.

paragraphs: Coverage: The authors manually selected 1,000 cases from 23 datasets across web agents, robotics, egocentric video, games and spatial planning.
Result: The best of 22 evaluated models reached 58.5% accuracy. Error analysis emphasized UI localization, motion interpretation, evolving state and 3D relationships.

sections.title: Interpretation

bullets.detail: Offline visual question answering is cheaper to compare than closed-loop execution, but cannot capture recovery, tool latency, policy violations or interactive exploration.
Add state-change questions to agent evaluation: what moved, what remains visible, which action changes state, and which UI element a proposed click actually targets.
